orswRecognition.title: Recognition from isolated extremal fixed points
orswRecognition.statement: For a contact Fano manifold with Pic(X) = ℤ[L], a reductive connected contact automorphism group of rank at least two, and isolated extremal components for a maximal torus, ORSW identify (X,L) with an adjoint homogeneous variety.
orswRecognition.encoding: The contract uses the actual analytic contact automorphism group, a compact real form, an inclusion-maximal compact torus, and the derivative-induced lift on the original contact line. Its conclusion is transitivity. The analytic-to-algebraic passage, algebraization of the action, and comparison of maximal tori remain part of the external corollary.
orswRecognition.locator: ORSW Theorem 5.1, p. 18; supporting comparison results listed below.

bwwRestriction.title: Restriction to extremal fixed components
bwwRestriction.statement: BWW give surjectivity of restriction of sections to an extremal fixed component; their small-dimensional result supplies at least two sections on a positive-dimensional component of dimension at most three.
bwwRestriction.encoding: The supplied analytic line is ample and generates the full Picard group. The same faithful holomorphic torus action, integral fiber character, and literal connected fixed component appear on both sides. Projectivity, GAGA, and algebraization of this particular line lift are external steps. No global generation hypothesis is inserted.

bwwReductive.title: The full twistor automorphism group
bwwReductive.statement: A positive quaternionic-Kähler twistor has a reductive holomorphic automorphism group. Its Kähler–Einstein metric supplies the Matsushima argument, while the full holomorphic automorphism group carries the usual complex Lie transformation-group structure.
bwwReductive.encoding: This combined contract provides a finite-dimensional complex Lie structure on the actual full automorphism group, with its specified topology, smooth joint evaluation, and the encoded reductivity condition. These transformation-group properties are part of the input, not inferred merely from a Lie-algebra dimension.
bwwReductive.locator: BWW v3, Theorem 6.6, p. 59; Salamon 6.1; Matsushima §1, Theorem 1; Kobayashi III §1, Theorem 1.1.

unique.title: Uniqueness of the contact distribution
unique.statement: In the Picard-generator case of BKK’s contact Fano trichotomy, the contact distribution is unique.
unique.encoding: Pulling the contact distribution back by any actual holomorphic automorphism therefore leaves its kernel unchanged. The contract states this preservation for every automorphism. Projectivity and the analytic/algebraic comparison belong to the external derivation.

ntComplexification.title: Infinitesimal contact complexification
ntComplexification.statement: On a positive quaternionic-Kähler twistor, the holomorphic contact Lie algebra is the complexification of the quaternionic isometry Lie algebra.
ntComplexification.encoding: The Lean statement specifies the actual natural lift of quaternionic isometries and its orbit differential. It requests a complex-linear bijection, with the differential compatibility needed by the development. The Lie-group and fixed-topology comparisons are included in the external statement.

isometryLie.title: The Riemannian isometry group is a Lie group
isometryLie.statement: The isometry group of a connected Riemannian manifold has its natural Lie-group structure and acts smoothly.
isometryLie.encoding: The specialization here is to the actual distance obtained from the supplied compact Riemannian geometry, on its existing compact-open topology. The conclusion includes smooth joint evaluation. This does not assert that every metric isometry preserves the quaternionic structure.

closedEmbedding.title: Closed subgroups inherit Lie structure
closedEmbedding.statement: A closed subgroup of a finite-dimensional Lie group is an embedded Lie subgroup.
closedEmbedding.encoding: For a continuous group homomorphism that is a closed embedding into the given real Lie group, the contract supplies a finite-dimensional real model, compatible manifold structure, Lie-group structure, and smooth embedding of the original topological group.

orbital.title: The compact symplectic orbital integral
orbital.statement: For the interleaved anti-Hermitian diagonal matrices X and Y, the normalized Haar integral of exp(tr(X g Y† g†)/2) equals cₙᵒᵈᵈ det[2 sinh(xᵢyⱼ)] / (Δᵒᵈᵈ(x) Δᵒᵈᵈ(y)).
orbital.encoding: The source is used for positive parameters and nonzero Vandermonde denominator. The code fixes the stabilizer of the interleaved symplectic matrix, normalized Haar probability, trace, determinant and constant. Their definitions are expandable below; passage to grouped coordinates is proved internally.

positiveContact.title: Positive contact geometry on the twistor
positiveContact.statement: The twistor of a positive quaternionic-Kähler manifold of quaternionic dimension at least two carries its natural complex contact geometry and the associated positive-Ricci structure.
positiveContact.encoding: The contract constructs a compatible complex atlas and nondegenerate holomorphic contact data on the actual sphere bundle, with the specified positive Ricci data. The original metric may have any positive scalar normalization; the chosen atlas must match the already defined almost-complex tensor.

kodaira.title: A positive line is ample
kodaira.statement: A positive Hermitian holomorphic line bundle on a compact complex manifold has a sufficiently high tensor power whose holomorphic sections give a projective embedding.
kodaira.encoding: Positivity is the explicit Chern-curvature test for a smooth Hermitian metric. AmpleCore refers to finite families of sections of powers of that same line and the resulting genuine projective embedding.
kodaira.locator: Wells VI §4, Theorem 4.1 and proof, pp. 234–240.

picardAlternative.title: Picard generator or contact homogeneity
picardAlternative.statement: BKK’s trichotomy leaves a Picard-generator case, projective space with its standard contact line, or a projectivized cotangent bundle of projective space.
picardAlternative.encoding: The two exceptional spaces are contact homogeneous. Combining this with the trichotomy and GAGA gives the encoded alternative: the original contact line generates the Picard group, or its actual contact automorphism group acts transitively.
picardAlternative.locator: BKK Proposition 2.3; LeBrun §2, Examples 2.1–2.2 and Proposition 2.3.

swEquation.title: The twistor Euler characteristic as an index
swEquation.statement: For nonnegative r, the twistor Euler characteristic χ(Z,Lʳ) is ⟨Â(M) ch(Symⁿ⁺²ʳ H), [M]⟩.
swEquation.encoding: The equality is between genuine sheaf cohomology and the development’s explicit Chern–Weil characteristic expression. The quaternionic class uses p₁(Q)/4 with representative −tr(FQ²)/(32π²), and integration uses the quaternionic orientation. Negative twists and later numerical bounds are not additional source assertions.
swEquation.relation: Index identity in the chosen normalization

swCohomology.title: Cohomology of powers of the contact line
swCohomology.statement: The twistor line has finite-dimensional cohomology, the Kodaira vanishing ranges and Serre duality; its holomorphic sections in degree one identify with complexified Killing fields.
swCohomology.encoding: The contract displays all ranges: higher cohomology vanishes for r ≥ 0, degrees at most 2n vanish for r < 0, and duality relates (r,s) to (−r−n−1,2n+1−s). The canonical-line isomorphism is a prerequisite. Hilbert values are derived later.
swCohomology.locator: Semmelmann–Weingart §2, pp. 2–3, the discussion surrounding equations (2.1)–(2.2).

ballmann.title: Positive anticanonical curvature gives simple connectedness
ballmann.statement: A compact connected complex manifold with positive anticanonical bundle is simply connected: the positive first-Chern class yields a positive-Ricci Kähler metric, and Kobayashi’s theorem applies.
ballmann.encoding: The line is the determinant of the actual holomorphic tangent bundle. The auxiliary Kähler metric need not equal the supplied Hermitian metric. The external chain includes the Chern-form interpretation and the Calabi–Yau consequence used by Ballmann.
ballmann.locator: §5.4 (5.59), p. 78; Theorem 6.12, p. 85; Corollary 7.3 and following discussion, pp. 88–89.

wolfLeBrun.title: Homogeneous twistor implies metric symmetry
wolfLeBrun.statement: Homogeneous contact geometry identifies the relevant twistor with that of a quaternionic symmetric space; the twistor determines the normalized positive quaternionic-Kähler metric.
wolfLeBrun.encoding: The combined corollary returns intrinsic symmetry of the given metric from a simply connected genuine twistor and transitivity of its actual contact automorphism group. Identification of the metric up to positive scale and preservation of point symmetries under scaling are part of the correspondence being assumed.
wolfLeBrun.locator: Wolf Theorems 5.4 and 6.1; LeBrun §2 and Corollary 3.4.

derdzinski.title: The four-dimensional positive Einstein case
derdzinski.statement: A compact oriented positive Einstein four-manifold with the specified vanishing Weyl half is isometric, up to scale, to the standard sphere or complex projective plane.
derdzinski.encoding: The contract packages the resulting global point symmetries, with the source’s orientation and curvature conventions translated to the actual metric. The development separately imposes the dimension-four Einstein/Weyl convention. This is an additional premise of both metric endpoints, outside the 15-field Sources record.

amann.title: The additional intersection sign for E14
amann.statement: Amann gives positivity of the signed pairing Q(x,y) = (−1)ʳᐟ² ∫ x ∧ y ∧ uⁿ⁻ʳᐟ² on even-degree cohomology, for the canonical quaternionic class u.
amann.encoding: Only a weaker, nonnegative square statement for some positive multiple of the actual Kraines class is requested. The positive-ray identification uses Semmelmann–Weingart; scaling to the analytic quarter class is proved internally. This premise is separate from Sources and occurs only in the E14 endpoints.
amann.locator: Amann v1, Theorem 1.2, p. 6; Semmelmann–Weingart §2, the Kraines-form normalization.
amann.note: The preprint version is explicit. The final journal text has not been directly compared; the Lean proof checks the implication from the displayed contract, not its fidelity to the paper.

c12.title: Metric symmetry through quaternionic dimension 12
c12.statement: For 1 ≤ n ≤ 12, every geometry satisfying the displayed compact connected positive quaternionic-Kähler encoding has a global point symmetry at every point of its given metric, conditional on Sources and the four-dimensional source.
c12.encoding: The endpoint is IsRiemannianSymmetric: a metric-preserving global diffeomorphism fixing each chosen point with derivative −id. In dimension four the input explicitly includes the Einstein/Weyl condition. Simple connectedness is not an input assumption.

e14.title: Metric symmetry through quaternionic dimension 14
e14.statement: The same metric-symmetry conclusion holds for 1 ≤ n ≤ 14, with the additional AmannInput premise.
e14.encoding: This is real dimension at most 56. The 15 shared contracts and four-dimensional source remain visible as arguments; AmannInput is the extra literature premise for this endpoint.

contact_c12.title: Generation of the original contact line through dimension 12
contact_c12.statement: For 2 ≤ n ≤ 12, Sources imply existence of a compatible twistor complex atlas and nondegenerate contact data whose original contact line is both globally generated and ample.
contact_c12.encoding: The conclusion concerns the original, unpowered line. The statement takes the shared Sources record; it has no separate four-dimensional hypothesis. Its displayed type, rather than a proof dependency minimization, determines the premises shown here.

contact_e14.title: Generation of the original contact line through dimension 14
contact_e14.statement: For 2 ≤ n ≤ 14, Sources and AmannInput imply existence of a compatible twistor complex atlas and nondegenerate contact data whose original contact line is both globally generated and ample.
contact_e14.encoding: The conclusion concerns the original, unpowered line. The statement takes the shared Sources record; it has no separate four-dimensional hypothesis. Its displayed type, rather than a proof dependency minimization, determines the premises shown here.

sources.title: The shared literature record
sources.statement: Sources is a conjunction of the fifteen named propositions shown in the Literature view. Constructing a value requires supplying all fifteen proofs.
sources.encoding: A definition of a proposition does not prove it. The final theorems accept this record as an argument. Methods named Sources.quaternionicSubmanifold, Sources.ntHamiltonian and other retired interfaces are now theorems, not additional fields.

QuaternionicSymmetry.Stage2IntrinsicGeom.statement: A compact connected positive quaternionic-Kähler geometry of real dimension 4n, with n ≥ 1. When n = 1, the record additionally requires the specified Einstein Ricci identity and the Weyl condition. These are geometric hypotheses of the target.
